summary: Feed s161_triple to NDR is degraded: 16.4% duplicates exceed 5% threshold, 92.9% encrypted bytes exceed NDR 90% tolerance, and VLAN 20 is missing with 50% packets untagged.

findings.root_cause: VLAN tags stripped upstream - SPAN/mirror configured as access port instead of 802.1Q trunk or packet broker stripping tags on ingress/egress, causing required VLAN 20 traffic to arrive untagged and invisible.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR loses segmentation context for required VLANs 10,20; cannot apply VLAN-aware detection policies and will miss lateral movement or policy violations in VLAN 20.

recommended_fix.why: Preserve/restore 802.1Q tags through TAP/SPAN and packet broker so NDR receives correctly tagged traffic for VLAN 20 and can enforce segmentation-aware detection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic aggregated from multiple SPAN/mirror sessions or TAPs without deduplication - same packet arriving via two paths and forwarded twice by packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes 16.4% of capacity on duplicates (444/2709), inflates flow counts, skews analytics/baselining and can cause false positives and missed true positives.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication with short time window to drop identical packets before delivery, restoring accurate traffic counts for NDR.

findings.root_cause: 92.9% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) - traffic forwarded without selective decryption or filtering, exceeding NDR's 90% encrypted tolerance.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for deep packet inspection; at this encryption level it is largely blind to C2, exfiltration, and exploit payloads, sharply reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Use broker/proxy selective decryption or add filtered feed of decrypted relevant traffic so NDR stays below 90% encrypted and regains payload visibility without violating privacy.
